source_text: Christum et a peccatis liberum non fuisse, sed carnis necessitate mentitum et aliis maculatum fuisse delictis
pass_a_gloss: Christ also was not free from sins, but by necessity of the flesh lied and was stained by other offenses.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: [They say that] even Christ was not free from sins, but was driven by the necessity of the flesh to lie and was stained by other offenses.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
